subject: cooper's hawk
title: A Hawk Learned That a Crosswalk Beep Means Cover for an Ambush

scenes.text: A hawk in New Jersey hunts by traffic light.
West Orange, winter 2021. A young Cooper's hawk, watched over 18 mornings by a zoologist.
The red light normally lasts 30 seconds. Press the crossing button and it beeps, the red stretches to 90, and the car queue grows ten houses long.
The hawk only showed up after the beep. It flew 65 meters along the sidewalk, under a meter high, hidden by the line of cars.
Then it cut between two cars into a yard full of sparrows and doves. Six attacks in 12 hours of watching.
The beep means a longer queue. A longer queue means cover. Next winter, an adult hawk was hunting the same way.

description:
A young Cooper's hawk learned that a pedestrian crossing beep means a long line of cars, and used the cars as cover to ambush birds.
In West Orange, New Jersey, zoologist Vladimir Dinets watched the hawk for 12 hours over 18 winter mornings in 2021 and 2022. The red light normally lasted 30 seconds; a pedestrian button extended it to 90 seconds and the queue grew long enough to shield a 65-meter low flight along the sidewalk to a yard full of sparrows and doves. The hawk appeared only when the signal sounded. The study was published in Frontiers in Ethology in 2025.
What's the smartest thing you've seen a wild bird do?
first_comment: When the crossing signal broke in 2023 and the residents stopped putting out food, the hawks never came back. Have you ever seen a wild animal use something humans built?
